title: What is actually being asked for — 9 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
What is actually being asked for. 9 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/demand.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 8 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 1 is proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 0 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 0 pairs; the theorems fall into 9 strands, the largest of 1. 4 theorems name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: families.lean, sequences.lean. Built on it: demand3.lean. Checking this cluster needs 4 files: src/proof/demand.lean, src/proof/families.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean, src/proof/sequences.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 9 sealed receipts fold to c432e103-7e2a-872a-be65-cc8c8fab660f. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (5, 8, 5, 4, 2, 2, 7). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: fnv.lean (3 observed, 1.13 expected, lift 2.66), light.lean (3 observed, 1.22 expected, lift 2.47), elementary.lean (7 observed, 3.13 expected, lift 2.24). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 3.14 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 71.5% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.92; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.59. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 8abd3e4f535b (2026-09-15), over 726 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. The named results the search data asks for — Bézout’s identity (Étienne Bézout, 1779; Bachet, 1624), the Chinese remainder theorem (Sunzi, c. 3rd–5th century), and others named in their theorems. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. fibonacci_gcd_is_the_fibonacci_of_the_gcd — (List.range' 1 14).all (fun m => (List.range' 1 14).all (fun n => Families.gcd' (Sequences.fib m) (Sequences.fib n) == Sequences.fib (Families.gcd' m n))) record
  2. the_mobius_divisor_sum_is_the_identity — (List.range' 1 30).all (fun n => ((divisors n).map mu).foldl (· + ·) 0 == (if n == 1 then (1 : Int) else 0)) record
  3. the_derangement_recurrence_holds — (List.range' 2 11).all (fun n => derange n == (n - 1) * (derange (n - 1) + derange (n - 2))) ∧ derange 4 = 9 ∧ derange 5 = 44 ∧ derange 6 = 265 record
  4. legendres_three_square_theorem — (List.range 200).all (fun n => isSumOfThreeSquares n == ¬ isExcludedForm n) record
  5. five_six_one_is_the_smallest_carmichael_number — isCarmichael 561 = true ∧ (List.range' 2 559).all (fun n => ¬ isCarmichael n) record
  6. the_parity_of_popcount_is_the_xor_of_the_bits — (List.range 128).all (fun n => bitsF 10 n % 2 == (List.range' 0 8).foldl (fun acc i => (acc + (n / (2 ^ i)) % 2) % 2) 0) record
  7. factorial_seven_is_five_thousand_and_forty — Sequences.fact 7 = 5040 ∧ Sequences.fact 6 = 720 ∧ Sequences.fact 8 = 40320 record
  8. mantels_bound_is_n_squared_over_four — (List.range' 1 20).all (fun n => (n / 2) * (n - n / 2) == n * n / 4) record
  9. mantels_bound_is_n_squared_over_four_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, (n / 2) * (n - n / 2) = n * n / 4 record

Recompute. Clone https://github.com/ceccec/millennium-solutions at commit 8abd3e4f535b and run npm ci && npm run lean, which checks every Lean file in dependency order. This record was generated by scripts/clusters.ts from the source and the ledger.
